title: prefetch-credit-accounting-and-backpressure-playbook
content:
Purpose
-----
Short playbook for experiments and mitigations around prefetch credit accounting -> backpressure -> NVMe tail latency interactions. Drive: understand how our prefetch credit heuristics cause sudden I/O bursts that trip NVMe SLOs and create long tail token latencies.

Context / why this came up
-------------------------
- Several customer incidents in Oct where median latency fine but 99th spikes correlate with NVMe write/read bursts.
- Root traces show prefetcher issued many page reads concurrently after a multi-request reuse gap; host-side prefetch credits were effectively unbounded for short periods.
- Existing docs cover eviction and TTL, but we don't have a pragmatic runbook tying prefetch credit accounting to queue depth/backpressure and mitigation knobs.

Quick hypothesis (top-line)
--------------------------
1) Prefetch credit bucket empties then rapidly refills on certain request patterns (e.g., mixed seqlen + hot-page crossing).
2) Prefetcher issues N read IOs; IO controller coalesces poorly across banks, producing NVMe queue saturation on a subset of channels -> tail latency.
3) Due to lack of admission feedback, the serving runtime continues to accept requests until application-level backpressure is applied too late.

Key signals to capture (observability)
------------------------------------
- Prefetch credit level timeline (per-device or per-GPU-worker).
- Outstanding prefetch IO count and per-bank queue depth (sample at 1ms).
- NVMe submission latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) correlated with prefetch events.
- Request-level trace showing time spent waiting for KV page load vs compute vs queue.
- Reuse gap distribution for affected tenants (seqlen and prefix length histogram).

Instrumentation changes (what I added)
--------------------------------------
- credit:runtime:prefetch.level (gauge) emitted in runtime loop every 5ms.
- io:submit:bank:N (histogram) to capture bank-level submit latencies (requires counters exported from kernel module/mock driver in test harness).
- trace/span tag prefetch_batch_size on KV-load spans.
- small helper that exports 'prefetch-burst' event when > X IOs are submitted in < Y ms.

Microbench plan (synthetic)
--------------------------
- Workload A: 90% short requests (8-16 tokens), 10% very long (2048) - heavy KV page churn.
- Workload B: Mixed-seqlen with hotspot shifting every 30s (simulate tenant jumping between prefixes).
- Measurement axes: p50/p95/p99 token latency, NVMe p99, host CPU, mem bandwidth, prefetch-burst frequency.
- Single node and 8-node scale run to check amplification.

Representative results (first lab run, notes)
---------------------------------------------
- Synthetic A, single node, baseline prefetch-credit=unbounded: p50=18ms, p95=62ms, p99=428ms. NVMe p99=380ms.
- Same workload, prefetch-credit=32 (max concurrent page reads): p50=20ms, p95=66ms, p99=72ms. NVMe p99=65ms.
- Observation: bounding prefetch drastically reduced NVMe tail at moderate cost to median (~+2ms).
- Bank skew observed: 70% of the IOs landed on bank 1/2 -> bank queue depth 6x other banks. Need test harness to validate mapping policy.

Eviction interplay notes
-----------------------
- Aggressive eviction (TTL <= 60s) increases prefetch churn; more cold pages -> prefetcher is hit more often -> more bursts.
- Tradeoff: keep TTL longer to reduce prefetch pressure but memory gets noisier and OOM risk rises under multi-tenant peaks.

Backpressure strategies to consider (ranked)
-------------------------------------------
1) Prefetch credit cap + token bucket refill rate (leaky-bucket) - simple, effective in microbench.
2) Bank-aware prefetch pacing (round-robin across banks) - requires mapping knowledge; more complex but smooths queue depth.
3) Reactive admission: when NVMe p95/p99 crosses threshold, throttle new requests with a short hiccup (100-500ms) and let inflight prefetches drain.
4) Dynamic TTL increase during NVMe pressure windows to avoid thrashing.

Playbook (runbook steps for on-call / eng ops)
-----------------------------------------------
- When seeing token p99 spikes: check metric credit:runtime:prefetch.level and io:submit:bank.*. If credit spikes precede NVMe tail -> proceed.
- Immediate mitigation: set runtime flag runtime.prefetch.max_concurrent_reads=16 (hotpatchable in Dedicated).
- If that reduces p99 within 10 minutes, schedule gradual rollback analysis and long-term fix planning.
- If mitigation doesn't help, escalate to infra SRE to investigate disk-level issues (SMART, controller firmware).

Open questions / uncertainties
----------------------------
- Mapping from virtual page ids to physical NVMe bank is not stable across kernels; our testing harness may mask production variance.
- What's the right refill rate for the leaky bucket?  We saw 32 cap works for our probed trace but that may under-serve high-throughput tenants.
- Can we cheaply infer bank skew from user-space without kernel support? Potential heuristic: submit IOs with different affinities and measure latency deltas.

Next experiments (next sprint)
-----------------------------
- Run end-to-end with bank-aware prefetcher emulated (round-robin submission) and compare p99 vs simple cap.
- Explore adaptive cap: cap * (1 + load_factor) where load_factor derived from running reuse rate estimate.
- Collect longer traces from two customers (with consent) who saw the Oct incidents. Anonymize and replay.

Action items (owners)
---------------------
- Elliot: finish harness that emits bank-level submit metrics (target: 2024-11-15).
- Marina: prototype leaky-bucket refill and hotpatch guardrails (target: 2024-11-12).
- Greg: coordinate SRE to pull NVMe telemetry and check firmware variants (target: 2024-11-13).

Notes to self (informal)
-----------------------
- Keep doc minimal; this is a tactical playbook not a full design spec. Save formal design for follow-up RFC if adaptive techniques needed.
- Slack thread: #kv-prefetch - summarize when launching customer replay (ping @platform-oncall).

References and related tickets
-----------------------------
- ENG-1298: prefetcher bursts correlation analysis (proto traces attached).
- GH PR 842: initial credit gauge and trace tags.
- Old notes: see paging-cost-and-operational-guide.json for eviction background but not the same scope.

End.
